title: The magic of Khmer classical dance | Prumsodun Ok

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The speaker delivers a talk explaining the history and gestures of Khmer classical dance. He demonstrates movements on stage and interacts with the audience.

lesson_structure.note: Introduction to the art of Khmer classical dance.
Explaining the physical curves and body posture.
Demonstrating four primary hand gestures and the cycle of life.
Demonstrating how gestures express words and emotions.

steps_taught.name: Tree gesture
steps_taught.description: A hand gesture representing a growing tree.

steps_taught.name: Leaves gesture
steps_taught.description: A hand gesture representing tree leaves.

what_works: Clear visual demonstration of hand gestures by the speaker.
what_hinders: Talk format instead of structured step-by-step dance instruction.

quotes.text: Robam Boran Khmer, or the art of Khmer classical dance, is more than a thousand years old.
Khmer classical dance is a transformation of nature.
The Khmer word for art, selapak, in fact, at its root means magic.
One student, one gesture, one dance at a time.

evidence_segments.observation: Speaker stands sideways on stage demonstrating curved posture, bent knees, and hyper-flexed elbows.
Speaker holds arm out showing four sequential hand gestures representing the cycle of life.

extraction.distinctive_method: Explaining dance vocabulary through a narrative of life cycles and nature while encouraging audience participation.
